transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hi Mr. Park. I wanted to come by and talk to you about the procedure we did on your arm earlier.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hi. Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, I need to discuss something that happened during the repair of the laceration.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was there a problem with the stitches?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The stitches are fine, but I made a mistake during the process. I didn't check your pain levels properly while I was working, and as a result, I completed the repair without giving you enough anaesthetic infiltration.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. I mean, it did hurt. A lot. I just thought maybe it was supposed to be like that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It wasn't. You should have been numb. I am very sorry that I didn't ensure you were comfortable, and that is my responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't really know what to say at the time. I've never really been in a hospital by myself before. I just figured you guys knew what you were doing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was just... it felt like it was going on forever, and I was just trying to breathe through it. I thought maybe if I complained it would make it take longer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. From a technical side, the infiltration is the liquid we inject to numb the area, and I didn't use enough of it or verify if it had worked before I started stitching.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you just forgot?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I failed to check your response. It was an error in my process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does that mean the wound is worse now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the repair itself is solid. But I know it was a painful experience.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yeah, it was. I'm still kind of shaking actually.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I don't really know if this happens often. Like, is this normal?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, this is not how we want to provide care. It shouldn't have happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I guess it's okay. I'm just glad it's over.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure we handle the recovery correctly now. I've written an order for a stronger pain medication to help you feel more comfortable for the next twelve hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the nurse bring that to you within the next twenty minutes. I want you to let the nursing staff know immediately if the pain spikes again or if you see any unusual swelling.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll also be back to check the dressing and your pain levels myself tomorrow morning around 8:00 AM.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'll let the nurse know to bring that medication now.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns and adjusts pacing to the patient's distress without interrupting.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and lay language was used, but the resident never checked for patient comprehension.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language ('I am very sorry') and explicitly took responsibility ('that is my responsibility').

R.justification: Resident used generic validation ('I understand') twice but did not name specific emotions back to the patient.

T.justification: Resident provided specific steps (medication, follow-up visit), timelines (20 minutes, 8:00 AM), a patient role (notify staff of pain/swelling), and addressed prevention by stating this is not how they want to provide care.
